title: Focus Board filtering follow-up
objective: Add a programmatically exposed filter control and completion summary to the applied primary interface.
requirements: FilterBar renders All, Active, and Completed native buttons in a group named Task filters, with aria-pressed true only for the current filter.

App initializes the current filter to all, delegates visible-task selection and completion counting to the applied query functions, preserves underlying task order and state, and displays {completed} of {total} complete.
Each filtered view keeps the semantic task list and shows concise filter-specific empty copy when it has no visible tasks.

files.task: Create the accessible three-option task filter control.
requirements: FilterBar renders All, Active, and Completed native buttons in a group named Task filters, with aria-pressed true only for the current filter.

owns.name: FilterBarProps
owns.description: Defines the selected filter and callback used to request a filter change.
owns.declaration: export interface FilterBarProps { current: "all" | "active" | "completed"; onChange: (filter: "all" | "active" | "completed") => void; }

owns.name: FilterBar
owns.description: Renders the accessible filter controls and reports selections through onChange.

context.purpose: Defines filter copy, programmatic selected state, and keyboard behavior.
Defines group naming and frozen filter class names.
Provides filter-group and filter-button classes including visible selected state.

skills.name: Accessible pressed-button group
skills.content: Import type { JSX } from react. Export exactly FilterBarProps and FilterBar with the planned signatures and `props` identifier. In FilterBarProps, repeat the exact inline union `"all" | "active" | "completed"` for both current and the onChange parameter; do not substitute a type alias. Render a div.filter-group with role=group and aria-label exactly `Task filters`. Render All, Active, and Completed as native type=button elements with class filter-button, aria-pressed comparing each exact lowercase ID to props.current, and onClick calling props.onChange with that ID.

constraints: Do not create custom keyboard handling for native buttons.
Do not edit CSS or another file.

requirements: App initializes the current filter to all, delegates visible-task selection and completion counting to the applied query functions, preserves underlying task order and state, and displays {completed} of {total} complete.

skills.name: Applied-interface extension
skills.content: Preserve the complete applied add-and-toggle interface and its imports, including import type { JSX } from react. Export only App with the exact planned signature. Add local filter state typed as `all | active | completed` and initialized to all. Import filterTasks and countCompleted from ./domain/task-query and delegate visible selection/counting. Import FilterBar from its exact supplied path and pass the filter state with the exact prop name `current` plus the setter with the exact prop name `onChange`; do not invent alternate prop names. Between composer and list render div.board-toolbar containing p.summary with `${completed} of ${tasks.length} complete` and FilterBar. Choose exactly one emptyMessage: `No active tasks.` for active, `No completed tasks.` for completed, and `No tasks yet.` for all. Pass filtered tasks, the existing toggle callback, and emptyMessage to TaskList. Do not render another empty-state paragraph in App; TaskList owns the sole empty message and always-present ul.

constraints: Pass filter state and its change callback through the exact FilterBar JSX prop names `current` and `onChange`.
Pass the visible collection, toggle callback, and empty-state copy through the exact TaskList JSX prop names `tasks`, `onToggle`, and `emptyMessage`.
Do not filter or reorder the underlying task state.
Do not edit CSS, other components, configuration, or another file.

skills.name: Single semantic empty state
skills.content: Preserve the applied named imports, ordered task mapping, TaskItem delegation, and always-present ul.task-list.
